season_compatibility: Workable only if T. Aman is harvested and the field drained early: high-yielding rabi crops need establishing by early December, but in the Polder 30/43/PSTU trials aman was harvested 12 Nov-10 Dec and land often stays flooded or saturated until December. Aman duration decides the gap: BRRI dhan62 100 d, dhan33 118 d, dhan72 125 d, dhan52 140 d. Hybrid maize Pacific 984 has a 135-day field duration. In Dacope (Khulna) 15 Dec sowing gave the best maize yield and sowing just after T. Aman harvest is advised with zero tillage.
water_implications: Polder 30 rabi crops relied on residual soil moisture and rainfall only (no irrigation after 2013 because canal water became unsuitable). Maize still gave 5.7-6.7 t/ha rainfed in the 2013-14 and 2015-16 dry seasons but was hit by both drought and excess rain in different years; Pacific 984 is listed as drought tolerant.
soil_nutrient_implications: Maize is a cereal following a cereal, with no legume credit. FAO ECOCROP: high maize yields make a heavy drain on soil nutrients and maize has a high nitrogen requirement, so N (and K) replacement must be planned.
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown. ECOCROP places maize tolerance at low salinity (<4 dS/m optimal, 4-10 dS/m absolute); in a Botiaghata trial salt-tolerant hybrid lines reached up to 11.37 t/ha.
waterlogging_implications: Maize is waterlogging-sensitive; T. Aman soils commonly stay saturated for about 15-45 days after harvest depending on topography, which delays sowing. Systematic sluice-gate drainage (terminal drainage by mid-November) is the stated prerequisite. About 500 mm of cyclone rain in May 2013 damaged all Polder 30 rabi crops.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Maize rice-equivalent yield 10.0 t/ha/yr vs Fallow-Rice-Rice 8.0 and farmers' fallow-rice-sesame 4-5; aman-rabi range 6.6-10.0 with maize highest and among the most stable.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna (system yield); Dacope, Khulna (sowing date); Botiaghata (salt-tolerant lines)
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Akther et al. 2024 JISCAR 42(1); JISCAR wheat waterlogging paper; FAO ECOCROP; SAU journal Botiaghata maize lines
notes: Sowing date of the Polder 30 maize plots is not stated in the source. Pest/disease break: no source found.

season_compatibility: Sunflower is sown by dibbling directly into wet soil right after T. Aman harvest (mid-November) in SRDI trials at Batiaghata, which avoids tillage delay. Hysun 33 has a 110-day field duration. Same early-drainage prerequisite as other rabi crops (establish by early December).
water_implications: Grown on residual moisture and rainfall in Polder 30; Hysun 33 is listed as drought tolerant. A BARI scientist states sunflower can be cultivated with two irrigations in the south of Bangladesh. FAO: deep root system (2-3 m) explores deep soil water.
soil_nutrient_implications: FAO general guidance (not site-tested): about 50-100 kg N, 20-45 kg P and 60-125 kg K per ha; crop is particularly sensitive to boron deficiency.
pest_disease_break: Sunflower is a susceptible host of Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (white mold); sclerotia survive 3-5 years in soil and cereals/grasses are non-hosts. Field flooding at warm temperatures destroys sclerotia, so a flooded T. Aman crop before sunflower is expected to help (inference from general evidence; not measured in Polder 30).
salinity_implications: Polder 30 topsoil salinity 2-16 dS/m; soil salinity is lowest Jul-Dec (monsoon and tidal water leach salts), intermediate Jan-Mar, and highest Apr-May (Polder 30 study). Rabi crops therefore meet rising salinity the later they are sown. FAO: sunflower emergence is 80-100% at ECe 0.7 dS/m, about 75% at 4.5, 30-60% at 9.5; later growth stages are moderately tolerant. Hysun-33 outperformed Local and BARI Sunflower-2 on saline land in Batiaghata and Chalna trials.
waterlogging_implications: Polder 30 rainfed sunflower (yield 1.0-2.9 t/ha) suffered drought or waterlogging depending on the year; a waterlogging tolerance value for sunflower was not found.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Sunflower rice-equivalent yield 8.5 t/ha/yr; aman-rabi with sunflower more stable across years than mungbean or sesame.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna; SRDI Salinity Management & Research Center, Batiaghata
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Financial Express (SRDI Batiaghata trial); FAO Land & Water sunflower page; UNB (BARI statement); PNW Handbook; NDSU
notes: Waterlogging tolerance value: no source found. Sclerotinia effect of T. Aman flooding is an inference.

season_compatibility: Traditional Polder 30 pattern (aman-mungbean). Mungbean was sown 8 Feb-16 Mar on residual moisture and harvested mostly 30 Apr-29 May; BARI Mug 6 field duration 65 days. This leaves a Dec-Feb fallow gap after aman. In Amtali (Barguna) mungbean followed mustard (sown 23 Feb, harvested 6 May) before T. Aus.
water_implications: No irrigation in Polder 30 rabi crops; poor germination, lack of irrigation and pre-monsoon rain kept yields at 0.4-0.9 t/ha. In Khulna coastal saline soil frequent pond irrigation raised BINA Mung-2 germination by more than 20%.
soil_nutrient_implications: Legume: the IAEA coastal pilot lists mungbean among crops that fix nitrogen and improve soil quality for subsequent seasons. The N benefit is mainly realised by the next crop (see Mungbean to Rice).
pest_disease_break: BARI Mug 6 is listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus. No rotation-specific pest/disease-break evidence found for rice to mungbean.
salinity_implications: BINA Mung-2 survived soil ECe 6.5-9.8 dS/m with irrigation water ECw 3.0-4.8 dS/m up to 45 days after sowing in Khulna coastal saline soil (topsoil salinity 3.8-13.8 dS/m Jan-May).
waterlogging_implications: Polder 30 mungbean and sesame were destroyed by waterlogging in 2012-13 after about 500 mm of cyclone rain in the last week of May; late-May rain is the key risk for a Feb-May mungbean crop.
system_yield_evidence: Khulna (Polder 30): Fallow-Rice-Mungbean rice-equivalent yield 8.8 t/ha/yr (aman-rabi range 6.6-10.0); aman-mungbean is a predominant existing Polder 30 system. Amtali: T. aman-mustard-mungbean-T. aus REY 14.16 t/ha.
region: Polder 30, Batiaghata, Khulna; Khulna coastal saline soil (SRDI/Khulna University)
source: Mondal et al. 2020 JISCAR 38(2); Saha et al. 2019 JISCAR 37(2); Bhuiyan et al. 2000 Khulna Univ. Studies; IAEA
notes: Mungbean here is a low-yield Feb-May crop; the value is mostly the nitrogen/soil benefit for the following T. Aman.
